title: Notre Dame's Washington Hall and the Legend of George Gipp's Ghost

sources.what: Gipp died at 3:23 a.m. Dec. 14, 1920, at St. Joseph Hospital, South Bend, age 25; tonsillitis, pneumonia, strep throat; Walter Camp picked him as Notre Dame's first All-American; no evidence he was locked out and slept on the steps; Rockne's 1928 Army talk at Yankee Stadium, 12-6; no evidence Gipp made the request
sources.who: Notre Dame Magazine, 'George Gipp's Galloping Ghost' (Dec. 14, 2020)

sources.what: died Dec. 14, 1920, age 25, strep throat infection and pneumonia; Notre Dame's first Walter Camp All-American; the locked-out story 'popular but apocryphal'; Rockne used the story to rally a 12-6 upset of Army in 1928; Washington Hall is 'the campus' theatre building'
sources.who: Wikipedia, George Gipp (and its cited sources)

sources.what: died Dec. 14, 1920, at 25 in South Bend; throat and lung infections and pneumonia; first Notre Dame All-American; Rockne's 1928 talk, beat Army 12 to 6

sources.who: The Observer (Notre Dame), 'Professor debunks ghost story' (2013)

beats.text: At Notre Dame, students say the old theater, Washington Hall, is haunted, many say by George Gipp.
beats.label: NOTRE DAME, INDIANA
beats.credit: Illustration, not the actual building. Sources: Notre Dame Magazine; The Observer

beats.text: In 1920, Gipp became Notre Dame's first Walter Camp All-American.
beats.label: THE GIPPER
beats.credit: Notre Dame Magazine; Encyclopedia of World Biography

beats.text: On December 14, 1920, he died after an illness reported as strep throat and pneumonia. He was 25.
beats.label: SOUTH BEND

beats.text: Legend says he got locked out after curfew and slept on Washington Hall's steps. There's no evidence of that.
beats.label: THE LEGEND
beats.credit: Legend: ND Admissions. History: Notre Dame Magazine; The Observer

beats.text: By 1921, students wrote of footsteps and a phantom horn, without naming Gipp. Years later, a student said he saw Gipp's ghost ride a white horse up its steps.
beats.label: WHAT STUDENTS SAY
beats.credit: The Observer (2013, 2016); Michael Kleen; Notre Dame Magazine

beats.text: In 1928, coach Knute Rockne said Gipp's dying wish was to win one for the Gipper. No one can prove Gipp said it. They beat Army, 12 to 6.
beats.label: NOTRE DAME VS. ARMY

beats.text: Today, some students say the Gipper never left.
beats.label: WHAT STUDENTS SAY

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: Round 1: line 2 to 'first Walter Camp All-American' (Gus Dorais was a 1913 consensus All-American); line 5 ties the horse to Gipp years later; room picture, shadow figure and orbs removed. Round 2: line 3 cause hedged; line 5 'Gipp's ghost ride a white horse' per the Observer; line 6 adds 'No one can prove Gipp said it'; the South Bend street picture replaced by a year card. Round 3 (34 claims): line 5 now says the 1921 reports didn't name Gipp; the drawing is marked as an illustration; all supported.
